title: SYNTHESIS, SPECTROSCOPIC CHARACTERIZATION, SOLVENT-DEPENDENT KETO–ENOL TAUTOMERISM, AND ELECTROCHEMICAL BEHAVIOR OF OXADIAZOLE- AND TRIAZOLE-LINKED β-KETO ESTERS
abstract: Four β-keto ester derivatives containing 1,2,4-triazole (A7 and A8) or 1,3,4-oxadiazole (A13 and A14) thioether units were synthesized by S-alkylation of the corresponding thiol/thione precursors with ethyl 4-chloro-3-oxobutanoate in ethanol using sodium acetate as a stoichiometric basic additive. The proposed structures are supported by FT-IR, 1H NMR, and 13C NMR data, including disappearance of the precursor S–H resonances and appearance of signals attributable to the β-keto ester fragment. Solvent-dependent keto–enol behavior was examined qualitatively by 1H NMR spectroscopy in DMSO-d6 and CDCl3 at 298 K. Only keto-form diagnostic resonances were resolved in DMSO-d6. In CDCl₃, A7 displayed signals of both keto and enol species; A8 and A14 displayed resolved enol-form signals without a resolved keto methylene signal; and A13 retained a resolved keto methylene signal without detectable enol resonances. UV/Vis spectra showed intense absorptions mainly in the ultraviolet region and weaker solvent- and concentration-sensitive features at longer wavelengths. Cyclic voltammetry in DMF containing 0.10 M tetrabutylammonium perchlorate revealed multiple cathodic processes that were predominantly irreversible on the experimental time scale. Because the Ag quasi-reference electrode was not calibrated against an internal ferrocene standard, the electrochemical results are interpreted comparatively within this data set rather than as absolute formal potentials. The combined results demonstrate qualitative relationships among heterocycle identity, methoxy substitution, solvent-dependent tautomeric signatures, and electrochemical response.

title: Process Optimization and Mass Transfer Characteristics of Ultrasound‐Assisted Curcuminoid Extraction From Curcuma caesia in Deep Eutectic Solvents
abstract: ABSTRACT The goal of the study was to examine how curcuminoids interact and mass transfer in deep eutectic solvents (DES) that have various physicochemical properties. The chosen DES systems were created to investigate how curcuminoid solubilization, extraction efficiency, and stability during ultrasound‐assisted extraction are affected by solvent polarity, acidity, viscosity, and hydrogen‐bonding interactions. The study also assessed the thermal stability of curcuminoids in various DES. Curcuminoids were extracted using ultrasound in five different DES, including binary mixtures of fructose, choline chloride, sucrose, and lactic acid. The lactic acid‐sucrose demonstrated higher total curcumin content (TCC), antioxidant activity, and total phenolic content (TPC). Consequently, the ultrasound‐assisted extraction method using lactic acid‐sucrose was optimized and modeled to achieve maximum TCC. The extraction of curcuminoids in lactic acid‐sucrose DES adhered well to a pseudo‐2nd‐order kinetic model. Compared to conventional methods, ultrasound‐assisted extraction in lactic acid‐sucrose showed a higher extraction rate, attributed to higher diffusivity and lower Biot and Schmidt numbers. Moreover, lactic acid‐sucrose DES exhibited enhanced thermal and pH stability for curcuminoids. This proposed extraction method presents an efficient and sustainable approach for extracting curcuminoids from black turmeric, with potential applications in the pharmaceutical and food industries.

title: Structural Core Discrimination of Emerging Synthetic Cannabinoids: A Presumptive Colorimetric Test
abstract: Abstract The continuous structural modifications of new psychoactive substances (NPS), particularly synthetic cannabinoids (SCs), present significant analytical challenges in their rapid identification. Following the discovery of a novel third-generation SC in seized herbal material with no matches in national databases, a simple analytical approach based on core structure recognition was developed. An effective yet straightforward colorimetric assay was developed to distinguish structural cores of SCs through their distinctive fluoride reactions. This method can clear distinguish between SCs containing isatin cores and those with indole or indazole moieties due to their distinct spectroscopic signatures. The method was validated against reference standards, demonstrating a strong linear relationship ( R 2 = 0.9998), high precision (relative standard deviation (RSD) < 2%), low detection limit (2.89 µM), and quantitative recovery (> 101%) from herbal matrices. To our knowledge, this is the first approach to identifying core structures of SCs prior to mass spectrometry analysis of unknown compounds, significantly streamlining their structural elucidation. Moreover, the net colour changes produced enable reliable, rapid detection of the compounds with the naked eye at concentrations representative of those found in seized herbal materials, making the method suitable for both forensic laboratories and rapid on-site screening by law enforcement agencies. This approach offers an effective solution for presumptive testing of emerging SC variants in both laboratory and field settings.

title: Translation fidelity mechanisms and their changes in aging
abstract: Abstract Protein errors (amino acid misincorporations) are associated to protein misfolding and misfunction, and lower levels correlate with longer lifespan 1 . Despite their prevalence, proteome-wide tracking of misincorporations in eukaryotes is challenging, with most insights being recent and coming from the mining of extensive proteomics data sets 2–5 . These experimental challenges have precluded the direct in vivo probing and full understanding of the bases of fidelity in higher eukaryotes, and their influence in complex processes such as aging. Here we measured proteome-wide misincorporation frequencies in two experimentally tractable eukaryotic systems, yeast and mouse, using mass spectrometry. We find translation fidelity is organism and organ specific. The measured error frequencies correlate with codon:anticodon pairing thermodynamics and tRNA pool composition, which can have synergistic or opposing effects on fidelity depending on organism or tissue type. Most identified protein errors carry a negative fitness burden. Aging experiments in our two systems reveal that, with age, error frequencies increase in post-mitotic cells, but not so in mitotic ones. These changes correlate with remodeling of the tRNA pool, which we identify as a crucial regulator of translation fidelity during lifespan.

title: Electrochemical Reduction of Acetonitrile to Gaseous C2 Products and Implications for Small Molecule Transformations
abstract: Acetonitrile (CH3CN) is a polar aprotic solvent that is widely used in electrochemistry due to its large dielectric constant, strong ability to solubilize numerous substrates and catalysts, and stability under a wide range of applied potentials. In the context of electrocatalysis, reaction rates and product selectivities can differ markedly in CH3CN relative to other solvents, but the possibility of solvent reduction remains poorly explored. Herein, we report that CH3CN is reduced electrochemically in the presence of organic acids to form ethylene, ethane, ethylamine and ammonia. To our knowledge, this study constitutes the first report of electrochemical acetonitrile reduction to ethylene and the first molecular system to generate ethane. These reactions are catalyzed by iron tetraphenylporphyrins but also occur on plain glassy carbon electrodes, highlighting the generality of this reduction to a variety of other catalyst systems. Isotopic labelling coupled with high‐resolution gas chromatography-mass spectrometry shows that CH3CN is the source of ethylene and ethane and offers insights into plausible mechanistic pathways. Because the observed hydrocarbons and amines are also desired products of CO2 or N2 reduction or C‒N coupling reactions, these observations motivate increased scrutiny as to the origin of unusual reduction products when electrocatalytic reactions are performed in CH3CN.

title: An integrated experimental–computational platform for evaluating blood–brain barrier permeability of novel kynurenic acid derivatives
abstract: Kynurenic acid (KYNA) is an endogenous neuroactive metabolite with considerable therapeutic potential, but its clinical translation is limited by poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability. Although numerous KYNA derivatives have been developed to improve brain delivery, the molecular determinants governing BBB permeability remain insufficiently understood. Here, we established an integrated experimental-computational platform for the rational evaluation and optimisation of BBB permeability in novel KYNA derivatives. The platform combines a validated UHPLC-MS/MS assay, experimental determination of lipophilicity using a modified shake-flask method, and computational prediction of protonation states, tautomeric equilibria, solvent-accessible surface areas, and BBB-related molecular descriptors. Targeted structural modifications markedly improved lipophilicity and BBB permeability compared with KYNA. Apparent permeability coefficients (Papp) ranged from 3.4 × 10⁻⁶ to 1.1 × 10⁻⁵ cm s⁻¹, with Compound 4a exhibiting the highest permeability (3.23-fold higher than KYNA), followed by Compounds 4b (2.57-fold) and 4d (2.11-fold). Experimental BBB permeability showed significant correlations with experimentally determined logD, predicted logBB, and solvent-accessible surface area descriptors. The superior permeability of Compound 4a was associated with a substantially higher population of the zwitterionic enol tautomer, suggesting a possible contribution of tautomeric equilibria to the observed permeability differences. Overall, this work establishes an integrated platform linking molecular structure, physicochemical properties, and BBB permeability to support the rational evaluation and prioritisation of compounds within the investigated KYNA derivative series. Among the investigated derivatives, Compound 4a showed the most favourable in vitro BBB permeability profile and therefore warrants further pharmacokinetic and in vivo evaluation.

title: Alternative synthetic pathways to selected molecular fluorophores present in citric acid-based carbon dots
abstract: Molecular fluorophores (MFs) are an integral part of many raw reaction mixtures prepared during the synthesis of carbon dots (CDs) from small organic molecules by the bottom-up methods. Despite their significant contribution to the luminescence of as-prepared CDs, the investigation of optical properties of MF is complicated by the pH dependence, possibility of formation of tautomers, low yields and complicated isolation. In this review, we summarize the structure of MFs detected in CDs prepared from citric acid (and various dopants), whose structure contains pyridin-2(1 H )-one ring annulated to 5- or 6-membered heterocycles. These compounds are closely related to citrazinic acid (CZA). The second part of the review deals with the alternative synthesis pathways towards ring-fused 2-pyridones, that could be used to prepare analogous compounds without the drawbacks related to the direct synthesis from CA (formation of carbonaceous matrix along with MFs resulting in low yields). MFs prepared by alternative pathways, free from polymerized and carbonized particles, could be used as standards towards better understanding of optical properties of CDs.

title: Antifungal metallacarboranes modulate Hsp90 activity
abstract: Aims Despite growing interest in metallacarborane biological activity, the molecular targets underlying their antifungal activity remain unknown. This study aimed to identify protein targets of antifungal metallacarborane derivatives in Candida albicans and to characterize their interaction with the molecular chaperone Hsp90.Experimental Affinity chromatography using chromatographic beads bearing immobilized [CoSAN-I]− was employed to pull down proteins from C. albicans cell lysate. Captured proteins were identified by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry. Direct binding of [CoSAN]−, [CoSAN-I]−, and its derivatives to recombinant Hsp90 was confirmed by affinity chromatography and surface plasmon resonance. The effect of compounds on Hsp90 ATPase activity was assessed using a malachite green phosphate release assay. Molecular docking and DFT (Density Functional Theory) calculations were performed to rationalize binding mechanisms.Results MALDI-TOF analysis identified 72 interacting proteins, of which 14 are established antifungal targets; Hsp90 showed the highest sequence coverage (82.7%). SPR confirmed direct, multivalent binding of all metallacarborane derivatives to Hsp90. The compounds modulated Hsp90 activity in a biphasic, dose-dependent manner, with maximal activation of 82–107% at 50–75 µM.Conclusions Metallacarboranes directly engage and functionally modulate Candida albicans Hsp90, establishing a novel mechanistic basis for their antifungal activity and providing a rational framework for the development of boron-cluster-based therapeutics.

title: A Solid-Phase Platform for Site-Specific Thiolation and Thioether Functionalization of DNA Oligonucleotides
abstract: Thionucleobases provide distinctive hydrogen-bonding, electronic, and photochemical properties, but their site-specific incorporation into DNA often requires specialized sulfurcontaining phosphoramidites and multistep monomer synthesis. Here, we establish a unified protocol using sodium hydrosulfide (NaSH) and 1,8-diazabicyclo[5.4.0]undec-7-ene (DBU) for direct on-support conversion of 8-bromo-2′-deoxyadenosine (Br 8 dA) to 8-thio-2′deoxyadenosine (s 8 dA), late-stage C8 thioether diversification, and concurrent conversion of Br 8 dA and 4-triazolylthymidine within a single DNA strand. Electrophilic precursor nucleosides were incorporated by standard solid-phase synthesis and subsequently converted while the oligonucleotide remained support-bound. Conversion of Br 8 dA to s 8 dA was first demonstrated using 2-(trimethylsilyl)ethanethiol and subsequently achieved directly with NaSH·xH2O, eliminating the need for a separate fluoride-mediated deprotection step. Substitution at the C8 was compatible with mixed sequences, multiple modifications, and a range of aliphatic and aromatic thiols, enabling late-stage installation of diverse sulfurcontaining functionalities. Application of the same support-bound protocol to 4-triazolylthymidine afforded DNA containing one or more 4-thiothymidine (s 4 T) residues, and both thionucleobases could be generated within the same strand. Products were characterized by strong-anion-exchange high-performance liquid chromatography and electrospray ionization mass spectrometry. This workflow shifts sulfur installation from specialized monomer synthesis to a simple late-stage conversion and provides practical access to site-specifically thiolated and C8-thioether-functionalized DNA.

title: Synthesis, Characterization, and Multimodal DNA Interaction of Novel Mn(II), Fe(III), and Co(II) Acylhydrazone Complexes
abstract: ABSTRACT A novel acylhydrazone Schiff base ligand was synthesized via the condensation of 2‐fluorobenzohydrazide with (2E)‐3‐(2‐methoxyphenyl)prop‐2‐enal and subsequently complexed with Mn(II), Fe(III), and Co(II) ions. We primarily characterized the resulting materials by thermal analysis (TGA‐DSC), elemental analysis, high‐resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (HRESIMS), and powder x‐ray diffraction (PXRD), complemented by FT‐IR and UV–vis spectroscopy, 1 H NMR, and complexometric titration, confirming the formation of stable, well‐defined coordination structures. DNA‐binding studies using absorption spectroscopy, viscosity measurements, and ethidium bromide displacement assays supported compound‐dependent, predominantly groove‐associated or mixed non‐covalent interactions rather than a classical intercalative binding mode. Fluorescence quenching and binding assays with bovine serum albumin (BSA) demonstrated measurable protein‐binding affinities, with the Fe(III) complex showing the highest experimental binding constant. Molecular docking complemented the experimental findings by suggesting distinct binding orientations and non‐covalent interaction patterns with DNA and BSA. For DNA, the predicted interactions included hydrogen bonding, halogen contacts, and π‐related interactions with nucleotides, whereas BSA docking suggested a probable binding region in the vicinity of Site II. The compounds also showed positive log P values, indicating a moderate lipophilic character. Collectively, the results demonstrate that metal coordination modulates DNA and BSA recognition, providing complementary insight into the structure–interaction relationships of these acylhydrazone complexes.

title: Barbiturate Derivatives for Stable Aqueous Nanoscale Pigment Yellow 150 Dispersions
abstract: Three structurally related barbiturate-derived dispersants were synthesized and evaluated to investigate how molecular architecture relates to the aqueous dispersion behavior of Pigment Yellow 150. BA-A and BA-B contain arylazo/hydrazone-type frameworks bearing nominal sulfonate and carboxylate termini, respectively, whereas BA-C contains an arylidene framework bearing a nominal carboxylate terminus. Their acid-form precursors were characterized by proton nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, and ultra-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. BA-A and BA-B produced Pigment Yellow 150 dispersions with z-average hydrodynamic diameters of 67.04 and 69.30 nm, polydispersity indices of 0.12 and 0.15, zeta potentials near -40 mV, and low apparent viscosities. In contrast, BA-C produced a coarse dispersion with a z-average hydrodynamic diameter of 1858 nm, while BYK-190 gave 124.70 nm at the tested nominal dosage. The BA-A and BA-B solutions exhibited calculated Washburn penetrativities approximately 2.5 times that of water, and their pigment dispersions showed dominant proton transverse-relaxation peaks at shorter times than the BA-C dispersion. Overall, BA-A and BA-B exhibited more favorable powder wetting and colloidal stabilization than BA-C, supporting a formulation-specific relationship between molecular architecture and dispersion performance within the investigated series.

title: Design, Synthesis, and Structural Characterization of Novel Nitrogen‐Bridged Heterocycles: Pyrazolo[3,4‐ b ]pyridine, Pyridopyrazolo[1,5‐ a ]pyrimidine, and Fused Furopyrimidine Derivatives
abstract: ABSTRACT Nitrogen‐bridged fused heterocycles represent important structural motifs in medicinal and synthetic chemistry. Pyridine‐ and pyrimidine‐containing fused systems are especially attractive due to their broad pharmacological potential and structural adaptability. A series of novel nitrogen‐bridged heterocyclic systems has been synthesized and structurally characterized. The study afforded new condensed frameworks, including pyrazolo[3,4‐ b ]pyridine, pyridopyrazolo[1,5‐ a ]pyrimidine, and a variety of triazolo‐, pyrazolo‐, and tetrazolo‐fused furopyrimidines. An efficient method for the synthesis of new heterocyclic systems, namely pyrazolo[3,4‐ b ]pyridine and pyridopyrazolo[1,5‐ a ]pyrimidine, was developed from 5,6‐dimethyl‐2‐oxo‐1,2‐dihydropyridine‐3‐carbonitrile. Moreover, o ‐alkylation and intramolecular cyclization of a pyridine chloro derivative provided a furo[2,3‐ b ]pyridine scaffold, which was converted into pyrido[3′,2′:4,5]furo[3,2‐ d ]pyrimidin‐4‐one. This intermediate was then transformed into the hydrazino derivative, serving as a versatile precursor for the synthesis of triazolo‐, pyrazolo‐, and tetrazolo‐fused furopyrimidines. The structures of the newly obtained compounds were confirmed by IR, 1 H and 1 3 C NMR spectroscopy, and elemental analysis. Selected derivatives were further characterized by mass spectrometry and x‐ray diffraction. The tautomeric behavior of tetrazole/azide systems and the rearrangement of triazole rings were investigated using spectroscopic methods, revealing dynamic equilibria and regioselective rearrangement. These results demonstrate that pyridine‐based scaffolds provide a versatile platform for constructing complex polycyclic heterocycles with potential synthetic and pharmacological relevance.

title: Syntheses, structural characterization and catalytic studies of N^O-donor (pyrazolyl-phenoxy)imine transition metal complexes in ethylene oligomerization reactions
abstract: The transition metal complexes of the general formula [Co (L1) 2 ] (Co1), [ Pd (L1) Cl] (Pd1), [ Ni (L1) 2 ] (Ni1) , and [ Ni (L2) 2 ] (Ni2) prepared by the reactions of the appropriate CoCl 2 , Pd(NCMe) 2 Cl 2 , and NiCl 2 metal precursors with the respective pyrazolyl-phenoxy-imine ligands; ((2-(3,5-dimethyl-1H-pyrazol-1-yl)ethylimino)methyl)naphthalen-2-ol (HL1) and ((2-(3,5-phenyl-1H-pyrazol-1-yl)ethylimino)methyl)naphthalen-2-ol (HL2) . The new compounds were structurally characterized using NMR and FT-IR spectroscopies, mass spectrometry, elemental analyses, and single crystal X-ray crystallography. The molecular structure of Ni2 depicts two bidentate (N^O) HL2 ligands around the nickel(II) metal center to form rare diamagnetic square planar complexes. On the other hand, ligand HL1 displays a tridentate N^N^O coordination to palladium(II) to give a mono-ligated palladium(II) complex Pd1 , consistent with the theoretically optimized structures using Density Functional Theory (DFT). Upon activation with EtAlCl 2 as a co-catalyst, complexes Co1, Pd1, Ni1 , and Ni2 form active catalysts in ethylene oligomerization reactions to produce mainly C 4 and C 6 oligomers, depending on the co-catalyst used. While the use of EtlAlCl 2 forms C 4 and C 6 oligomers, MAO and Me3Al results in the dimerization reactions to afford mainly C 4 oligomers. Both the catalytic activities and product selectivity were controlled by the nature of the metal complex and reaction conditions. For example, the nickel-based complexes displayed higher catalytic activities of up to 46 120 g product mol –1 Ni h –1 compared to the other metal complexes. Similarly, the use of Ni2 /EtAlCl 2 catalyst system displayed the highest catalytic activity compared to the Ni2/ AlMe 3 and Ni2 /MAO systems.

title: Furan-Based Hydrazone-Linked Quinazolin-4-amine Hybrids: Design, Synthesis, Spectroscopic Validation, DFT Reactivity Analysis, and Keap1-Targeted Antioxidant Studies
Novel Ibuprofen Derivatives Bearing Thiadiazole Moiety: In Silico Study, Synthesis, and Preliminary Cytotoxicity Evaluation
abstract: The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is a receptor tyrosine kinase that is commonly upregulated in malignancies, including breast, pancreatic, and non-small-cell lung cancer. In this study, a new series of ibuprofen derivatives was synthesized and structurally characterized using FTIR, 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR and mass spectrometry. The final compounds were evaluated for antiproliferative activity against the lung adenocarcinoma cell line (A549) using the MTT assay. The compounds were also tested against normal human lung fibroblast (MRC-5) to determine their selectivity toward cancer cells. Gefitinib was used as a positive control. Among the tested compounds, compound MA3 exhibited potent cytotoxic activity against the A549 (IC50 = 4.002 µM) compared to gefitinib (IC50 = 20.65 µM). Interestingly, compounds MA1 and MA3 showed selectivity for cancer cell lines over MRC-5 cells. Molecular docking analysis suggests that compound MA3 may have an inhibitory effect through the formation of stable hydrogen bonds with the amino acid residues Met793 and Asp855, as well as a π-cation interaction with the Lys745 residue. ADME investigations confirmed that all compounds exhibited high bioavailability scores. Ultimately, compound MA3 was demonstrated to be a candidate for further preclinical investigations.

title: Design, Computational Study, Synthesis, Characterization and Anti-diabetic Evaluation of Novel N-Substituted Thiazolidinedione Derivatives
abstract: In the present study, a series of novel N-substituted 2,4-thiazolidinedione derivatives (PB-TZD1–PB-TZD14) were rationally designed, synthesized and evaluated for their antidiabetic potential. The synthesized compounds were characterized by FT-IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR and mass spectrometry. Molecular docking revealed favourable interactions of the synthesized derivatives with key residues of the PPAR-γ receptor, particularly Cys285. In vitro glucose uptake studies revealed that PB-TZD1 (36.00%), PB-TZD3 (34.30%) and PB-TZD6 (33.53%) exhibited significantly higher activity compared to the standard drug pioglitazone (24.77%). Among these, PB-TZD3 exhibited the most pronounced glucose-lowering effect in in vivo antidiabetic studies using a high-fat diet STZ-induced rat model. Adipocyte differentiation studies showed that PB-TZD3 significantly enhanced adipogenesis at higher concentrations, consistent with PPAR-γ activation. In silico ADME and toxicity predictions suggested favourable drug-like properties; however, these findings are preliminary and require further experimental validation. The structure–activity relationship analysis indicated that electronic, steric and hydrophobic factors play a crucial role in modulating biological activity. This study identifies PB-TZD3 as a promising lead compound and highlights the significance of N-substitution in optimizing thiazolidinedione derivatives for improved antidiabetic activity.

title: Development of oxygenase biocatalysts for the production of synthetically useful cis-diol compounds
abstract: The cis¬-dihydrodiol compounds, produced by the highly regio- and stereo-selective Rieske non-heme iron oxygenases, such as toluene dioxygenase (TDO), are versatile synthons for chiral, asymmetric synthesis. The cis-dihydroxylation of ortho- and meta-substituted phenols by TDO produce cyclohexenone cis-diols. The keto group of cyclohexenone cis¬-diol tautomers increases the functionalisation and stability compared to other arene cis-dihydrodiols. (4S,5S)-dihydroxy-3-iodocyclohexe-2-en-1-one, formed from 3-iodophenol by the TDO-expressing bacteria Pseudomonas putida UV4 and Escherichia coli LK, has been identified as a highly versatile synthon for chemoenzymatic synthesis. Earlier attempts at the production of significant quantities of this compound had been unsuccessful, due to its biodegradation by P. putida UV4. E. coli LK accumulated the target compound but struggled with substrate toxicity and formation of toxic catechol metabolites, which inhibit toluene dioxygenase. The project aimed to optimise the biotransformation of 3-iodophenol by P. putida UV4 for the production of preparative amounts of (4S,5S)-dihydroxy-3-iodocyclohex-2-en-1-one, eventually producing the compound in multigram quantities (~15 g). Additionally, catechol-2,3-dioxygenase (todE) of P. putida UV4 was introduced to E. coli LK, creating a strain able to degrade catechols. This new strain carries the todE gene on a Lac operon regulated pMCL210 plasmid and was designated E. coli 1/210LK. After optimisation of the biotransformation, it showed an increase in the concentration of (4S,5S)-dihydroxy-3-iodocyclohex-2-en-1-one of ~40% compared to E. coli LK, thus competing with P. putida UV4 but at a lower reaction rate. Using AutoDock (Vina), an analysis of the active site of TDO and its substrate interactions provided a rationale for earlier results and predicted new synthetically useful tricyclic cis-dihydrodiol metabolites. Molecular docking showed His311 and Gln215 as primary interaction partners for the orientation of phenols within the active site. Hydrogen bonding between the phenolic OH group and the side chain of Gln215 was highlighted as a possible reason for the formation of catechols via 1,2-dihydroxylation of phenols. Several tricyclic arenespreviously found to be acceptable substrates for naphthalene dioxygenase were also successfully docked to TDO. Dibenzofuran, dibenzothiophene and carbazole were biotransformed by P. putida UV4, fluorene was not. The dibenzofuran cis-dihydrodiol was produced in high yields (>60%). This project produced an improved biocatalyst, E. coli 1/210LK, for the production of cyclohexenone cis-diols, serving as basis for future research. Molecular docking has given insight into the active site and its substrate interactions, paving the way for further analysis. Molecular docking also predicted the formation of dibenzofuran ¬cis-dihydrodiol, which was applied in the total synthesis of ribisins A-C by Dr. C. McGivern.

title: Synthesis, Characterisation and Biological Evaluation of Some 5- Trifluoromethylisoxazole Derivatives
Ferrier Rearrangement Intermediates Featuring Aliphatic Acyl Protecting Groups
abstract: The Ferrier rearrangement of 1,2-unsaturated monosaccharides (glycals) to 2,3-unsatured glycosides, is important for the synthesis of pharmaceuticals and natural products. Mechanistically, the nucleophilic substitution proceeds via a cationic intermediate, the “Ferrier cation”, whose structure is difficult to capture with conventional analytical techniques. Here, we characterize the Ferrier cations of glucal and galactal building blocks involving aliphatic acyl protecting groups (pivaloyl-, levulinoyl- and chloroacetyl esters) using cryogenic gas-phase infrared spectroscopy. Comparing experimental and computed spectra of candidate structures, we established that all intermediates are stabilized by interactions of the C4 acyl protecting group with the C3 carbon of the pyranose ring (neighboring participation), potentially steering the stereochemical outcome of the Ferrier rearrangement. The resulting C4-C3-dioxolenium ion structure appears to be general to aliphatic acyl protecting groups, contributing to our fundamental understanding of Ferrier rearrangement reactions.

title: Analysis of neonicotinoid pesticides and their metabolites by liquid chromatography–electrospray ionization–tandem mass spectrometry
abstract: Neonicotinoid insecticides were first introduced in the 1990s as an alternative to older, more toxic types such as organophosphates, carbamates, and chlorinated hydrocarbons and have since become the most widely used class of insecticides globally. However, their use comes at a significant cost due to high toxicity to pollinators such as bees, beneficial predatory insects, and even insectivorous birds. To further the study of neonicotinoid effects, we developed a method for the LC-ESI-MS/MS (liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization-tandem mass spectrometry) analysis of imidacloprid, clothianidin, and nitenpyram. Standards enabled optimization of tandem quadrupole (MS/MS) detection for specific multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) method fragmentations and separation was achieved by UPLC (ultra-high performance liquid chromatography). However, mammalian samples that tested positive for neonicotinoids on enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs) disclosed none of the parent compounds by the LC-ESI-MS/MS method. Upon researcher request, neonicotinoid metabolites 6-hydroxynicotinic acid; 2-chloro-1,3-thiazole-5-carboxylic acid; 2-imidazolidone; 6-chloronicotinic acid; imidacloprid urea; imidacloprid olefin; desnitro-imidacloprid; and 5-hydroxyimidacloprid were included. The method was validated for linear response, limits of detection/quantitation, retention time stability, instrumental carryover, intraday- and interday-precision, standard curve stability, accuracy, and specificity. Limits of quantitation were measured at 0.1 ppb for the majority of compounds, although desnitro-imidacloprid and 5-hydroxyimidacloprid ranged above 1 ppb. The method was applied to extracted produce samples as a pilot study to test the method's utility. Red grapes contained imidacloprid, while pickles contained imidacloprid and clothianidin. Of concern to researchers studying the collapse of honeybee colonies, two of four samples of honey contained the imidacloprid metabolite 6-hydroxynicotinic acid at levels above 5 ppb.

title: Tandem-Affinity Crosslinking Mass Spectrometry Supports a Model of a DNA-PKcs–PP6 Regulatory Complex
abstract: Protein complexes can be modeled with data arising from crosslinking mass spectrometry, but it is difficult to collect such data from cellular sources, particularly for proteins that are part of extensive interaction networks. Here, we present a tandem-affinity purification crosslinking mass spectrometry (xTAP‑MS) method that enables structural analysis of low-stoichiometry complexes directly from cellular lysate. Applying this approach to the DNA-PK/protein phosphatase 6 (PP6) interaction, we selectively enriched endogenous DNA-PK/PP6 assemblies and generated inter- and intra-protein crosslinks suitable for the generation of a working model of the structure. Integrating crosslinking data with AlphaFold3 modeling positions the PP6 holoenzyme at the base of the DNA-PKcs HEAT-repeat cradle, proximal to a major autophosphorylation loop yet spatially compatible with kinase activation. Structure-guided truncations and mutagenesis of PPP6R3 are consistent with the model. Together, these results establish xTAP‑MS as an effective bridge between interactome discovery and mechanistic structural analysis, generating testable hypotheses for subsequent investigations.

title: A Rapid Liquid Chromatography–Tandem Mass Spectrometry Bioanalytical Method For Quantification Of Gepirone In Rat Plasma Using Lurasidone As An Internal Standard: Method Development, Validation And Pharmacokinetic Application
abstract: Gepirone is an azapirone antidepressant that acts primarily through partial agonism of serotonin 5-HT1A receptors and has gained renewed attention following its approval for major depressive disorder.This study designed to create a simple and reliable Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry procedure for determining gepirone in rat plasma using lurasidone as the internal standard.Chromatographic separation was accomplished on a Zorbax SB C18 column (150 × 4.6 mm, 3.5 μm) under isocratic conditions with methanol and 0.1% aqueous formic acid (40:60, v/v) at a flow rate of 1.0 mL/min.Detection was carried out on a SCIEX QTRAP 5500 mass spectrometer operated in positive ESI and multiple-reaction-monitoring modes.Plasma samples were prepared by protein precipitation, providing a rapid and economical sample-processing approach.The assay was linear over 10-80 ng/mL, with 0.9998 determination coefficient.All validation results satisfied the predefined requirements for selectivity, precision, accuracy, recovery, matrix effect, ruggedness, carryover, dilution integrity, and stability.Gepirone recovery ranged from 96.05% to 97.16%, whereas lurasidone recovery was 97.31%.Mean accuracy during matrix-effect assessment was 96.05% at the low quality-control level and 97.11% at the high qualitycontrol level.The RTs of gepirone and lurasidone were approximately 2.23 and 4.02 min, respectively, within a total analytical time of 7 min.The method was successfully applied to rat plasma samples and provided adequate performance for preclinical PK analysis.Its straightforward extraction, consistent recovery, and reproducible analytical response support its use for routine determination of gepirone in biological samples.

title: Insights into the Collision-Induced Dissociation Fragmentation Pathways of Sulfonamides: Loss of SO2 versus Intramolecular Oxygen Transfer
The Development of a Simple Liquid Chromatography‐Precursor Ion Scan‐Mass Spectrometry Screening Method for the Detection of Phytocannabinoids in Plant Extracts
abstract: ABSTRACT Screening of major cannabinoids in cannabis‐derived extracts is needed when these extracts are applied in pharmacological and biological studies. Precursor ion scan‐mass spectrometry (PIS‐MS) is a viable approach for the detection and screening of major cannabinoids through characteristic MS/MS fragmentation behavior. A PIS‐MS method was developed utilizing electrospray ionization (ESI) operated in the positive ion mode on a triple quadrupole‐linear ion trap mass spectrometer (QTRAP 6500). Three cannabis extracts were screened based on established MS/MS fragmentation pattern. Characteristic product ions at m/z 193.1 and 233.1 were optimized for PIS‐MS analysis. In addition, tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) was performed to aid in the putative identification of unknown cannabinoids, whereas authentic standards were used, when available, to confirm the identity. A quadrupole‐Orbitrap (Exploris 240) mass spectrometer equipped with ESI was also utilized to provide accurate mass measurements for single‐stage and MS/MS analyses, supporting the proposed structures of cannabinoids and their product ions. PIS‐MS complemented with high‐resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) analysis revealed the existence of six major cannabinoids in two plant extracts, and nine in the third one. Among the detected phytocannabinoids, an unexpected cannabinoid, namely, sesquicannabigerol (Sesqui‐CBG), was also identified among the most abundant ones. The MS/MS fragmentation behavior in both positive and negative ionization for Sesqui‐CBG was established for the first time, supported by accurate mass measurements and second‐generation MS/MS (MS 3 ) experiments. In conclusion, PIS‐MS provided an effective approach for the screening of abundant cannabinoids in plant products intended for therapeutic applications. MS/MS and accurate mass measurements confirmed the putative identification of detected cannabinoids. A comprehensive study for Sesqui‐CBG was performed, elucidating its fragmentation pathways and product ions.

title: Ultra-High-Performance Liquid Chromatography-High Resolution Mass Spectrometry and Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry Screening of Classical Psychoactive Substances, Novel Psychoactive Substances, and Metabolites in Postmortem Urine Samples
abstract: The use of new psychoactive substances (NPS), whether pure or in mixtures, has grown steadily, increasing the need for accurate confirmatory analysis in biological matrices given their chemical diversity, structural variability, and potential postmortem redistribution and degradation. Forensic interventions require comprehensive, broad-coverage screening strategies. Two complementary platforms, ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC-ESI(+/-)-Orbitrap-HRMS) and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), were used to screen classical psychoactive substances (CPS), NPS, and their metabolites in 25 postmortem urine samples with suspected consumption of NPS, using Platform-specific sample preparation and identification workflows. Forty-four drugs/metabolites were identified. Ketamine was the most prevalent drug (92% LC-MS, 84% GC-MS), along with its phase I metabolites norketamine, hydroxyketamine, and hydroxynorketamine. Cocaine (68% LC-MS, 12% GC-MS) and its main metabolite, benzoylecgonine (88% LC-MS, 52% GC-MS), were also frequent on both platforms, while amphetamine-type drugs, benzodiazepines, and opioids showed marked technique-dependent detection (e.g., 3,4-methylenedioxyamphetamine: 32% LC-MS, 4% GC-MS). UHPLC-ESI-Orbitrap-HRMS provided broader polarity coverage of parent drugs and metabolites; GC-MS reliably detected parent drugs and derivatizable xenobiotics. Combined use of both platforms provided complementary, high-confidence coverage for forensic toxicology urine screening; quantitative validation and larger cohorts are needed for diagnostic, impairment, and epidemiological extrapolation.

title: Development and Validation of a Novel Ultraperformance Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry Method for Serum 3-Epi-25-Hydroxyvitamin D 3 , 25-Hydroxyvitamin D 3 , and 25-Hydroxyvitamin D 2
abstract: Background: The epimeric form of 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 (3-epi-25-hydroxyvitamin D3, 3-epi-25-OH-D3) can interfere with the accurate measurement of total vitamin D. Therefore, reliable quantification of epimeric metabolites is important for improving measurement accuracy.Here, we developed and validated a novel laboratory-developed test (LDT) based on an ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) assay to measure the concentrations of 3-epi-25-OH-D3, 25-OH-D3, and 25-OH-D2 in serum.Methods: Sample pretreatment included derivatization with the PTAD reagent (4-phenyl-1,2,4-triazoline-3,5-dione).The assay was performed using the Shimadzu LC-40D UPLC system (Shimadzu, Japan) and Sciex Triple Quad 5500+ QTRAP Ready MS/MS system (Sciex, USA), with a total runtime of 16 minutes, flow rate of 0.15 mL/min, and serum volume of 100 µL.We evaluated the accuracy, precision, linearity, limit of detection (LOD), lower limit of quantification (LLOQ), carryover, and matrix effects.The results were compared with those obtained using the MSMS Vitamin D kit (PerkinElmer, Finland).Results: The precision and accuracy were all within acceptable limits.The verified linear ranges were 0.30-24.70,0.29-137.00,and 0.29-137.00ng/mL with LLOQs of 0.30, 0.29, and 0.29 ng/mL for 3-epi-25-OH-D3, 25-OH-D3, and 25-OH-D2, respectively.No significant carryover or matrix effects were observed.The method comparability for the MSMS Vitamin D kit was excellent, validating the transition to the new platform.Conclusions: This novel LDT UPLC-MS/MS assay showed acceptable analytical performance for measuring the serum concentrations of 3-epi-25-OH-D3, 25-OH-D3, and 25-OH-D2 and may help improve the accuracy and comparability of total vitamin D measurements, particularly in largescale epidemiological studies.

title: Elucidation of Fragmentation Pathways of Zolmitriptan and Eliglustat by Protonated ion High-Resolution QTOF-MS/MS for Highly Accurate Identification and Structural Characterisation
abstract: Introduction: Zolmitriptan is a Serotonin 5-HT1D receptor agonist developed for the oral treatment of acute migraine. Eliglustat is an oral substrate-reduction therapy used as firstline treatment for Gaucher disease type 1 (GD1). To date, the analytical work available on these drugs is largely confined to forced degradation studies analysed by liquid chromatography– tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS). Hence, in the present study, the protonated ions ([M+H]+) of Zolmitriptan and Eliglustat were investigated using UPLC coupled with a highresolution mass analyzer, specifically a Q-TOF analyzer with an Electrospray ionization (ESI) source, using collision-induced dissociation (CID) fragmentation. Methods: UPLC H-Class coupled to a Xevo G2-Xs Q-TOF mass spectrometer equipped with an ESI source in the positive ion mode was used for the analysis. Water and acetonitrile as mobile phase in a gradient program mode of elution and C18 column as stationary phase was used for UPLC. Results: Reasonable fragmentation paths were suggested for protonated ions of Zolmitriptan and Eliglustat, and the elemental compositions of the resulting ions were accurately described by the experimental results of UPLC QTOF-HRMS/MS analysis. This study calculated mass errors for molecular ions below 5.0 ppm and fragment ions below 15.0 ppm. Discussion: The unique fragmentation pathways obtained from the HR QTOF-MS/MS study made it easier to analyse and interpret the stability and potential degradation pathways of the protonated ions of Zolmitriptan and Eliglustat. Emerging approaches such as Electron-Activated Dissociation (EAD) offer enhanced capabilities for differentiating structurally similar or isomeric species and may provide complementary insights beyond conventional collision-induced dissociation. While such techniques were not within the scope of the present investigation, they represent a promising direction for future studies focused specifically on isomer characterization. Nevertheless, the current HRMS/MS-based fragmentation-mapping strategy presented here provides a robust and reliable foundation for the structural elucidation of the investigated molecules. Conclusion: The prediction of the most probable mass fragmentation pathways for both Zolmitriptan and Eliglustat and the formation mechanisms of the fragment ions enable a higher degree of certainty in their identification and hence make this method appropriate for quality control of these drugs and future research studies.

title: Recent advances in underwater in situ mass spectrometry: instrumentation, deep-sea applications, and challenges
abstract: The ocean is a major component of the Earth system and contains abundant biological, mineral, and energy resources. Conventional laboratory-based analytical methods are limited in underwater environments because sample collection, preservation, and transportation can alter the original chemical composition. In contrast, underwater in situ mass spectrometry enables adaptive sampling and analysis across temporal and spatial dimensions, achieving real-time feedback for in situ , long-term monitoring while significantly reducing labor and material resource consumption. These technologies facilitate qualitative and quantitative monitoring of dissolved gases in aquatic systems, characterized by rapid response and high sensitivity. These systems provide important analytical support for marine environmental monitoring, biogeochemical studies, and resource exploration. This review outlines the core components of underwater in situ systems, including membrane introduction systems, ionization systems, and miniaturized mass spectrometers. Recent advances in membrane introduction, water-vapor removal, ionization strategies, miniaturized mass analyzers, deep-sea field deployment, and recent integration of micro gas chromatography with mass spectrometry are critically summarized. Current challenges, including water-vapor interference, membrane fouling, calibration drift, power consumption, and long-term autonomous operation, are also discussed.

title: High-resolution FAIMS-mass spectrometry for breath analysis using atmospheric pressure chemical ionisation
abstract: Exhaled breath containing volatile organic compounds (VOCs) can be analysed non-invasively and has potential applications in disease diagnosis. Previous high-field asymmetric waveform ion mobility spectrometry (FAIMS)-based breath studies have primarily used low-resolution FAIMS with ion current detection rather than mass spectrometry (MS). Here, atmospheric pressure chemical ionisation (APCI) was coupled with high-resolution FAIMS-MS for direct breath analysis. APCI-FAIMS-MS increased the number of detected breath features by >200% compared with APCI-MS alone and consistently detected 60-130 breath features per sample. Within-participant heatmap consistency was comparable across the four participants based on structural similarity index analysis. Exploratory principal component analysis showed participant-associated clustering of breath profiles. These results demonstrate that high-resolution FAIMS substantially enhances breath feature detection and provides an orthogonal separation dimension for untargeted breath profiling. Future studies involving larger cohorts and disease-specific populations will determine whether the increased breath feature coverage afforded by high-resolution FAIMS can improve VOC-based classification and diagnostic performance.

title: Ganglioside profiling by ion mobility and mass spectrometry imaging identifies distinct biomolecular isomers in Niemann-Pick Disease
abstract: Abstract Gangliosides are glycosphingolipids implicated in the neurodegenerative pathology of Niemann-Pick disease type C2 (NPC2 disease), where accumulation of GM2 and GM3 is a hallmark of disrupted lipid trafficking and disease progression. Some gangliosides are structural isomers with identical molecular composition and mass, making them difficult to distinguish by mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) alone and leaving their spatial distributions unresolved. To address this challenge, we combined ion mobility spectrometry with mass spectrometry imaging for isomer-resolved ganglioside analysis. We assessed ganglioside complexity in wild-type ( Npc2+/+ ) and NPC2-deficient mice with or without AAV-BR1-mediated NPC2 gene therapy ( Npc2-/- AAV-BR1-NPC2 and Npc2-/- vehicle) using matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization (MALDI) MSI, and imaging-parallel reaction monitoring-parallel accumulation serial fragmentation (iPRM-PASEF-MS/MS) for in situ brain tissue analysis. Trapped ion mobility spectrometry (TIMS) enabled gas-phase separation of isomeric gangliosides, while iPRM-PASEF-MS/MS facilitated structural discrimination based on diagnostic fragment ions and identification of molecular modifications. Brain sections were analyzed by MALDI-MSI at 20μm spatial resolution, with selected regions examined using post-ionization imaging by MALDI-2 at 5μm. 59 mobility-resolved ganglioside features representing 23 putative annotations were identified, including separation and spatial mapping of GM1a/GM1b and GD1a/GD1b isomers. Notably, unreported modifications of gangliosides were identified, including GM1 fucosylation in Npc2 -/- mice and GD1 O-acetylation exclusively detected in Npc2 +/+ mice. Spatial ganglioside profiling by MSI demonstrated that gene therapy of Npc2 -/- mice partially restored normal ganglioside localization in brain, indicating modulation of lipid storage. This study establishes isomer-resolved lipid imaging for investigating ganglioside alterations in disease models and the effects of therapeutic intervention.

title: Characterization of the Chemical Constituents in Shenyanshu Tablets by Ultra‐High‐Performance Liquid Chromatography Quadrupole Time‐of‐Flight Mass Spectrometry
abstract: Shenyanshu tablets (SYST), a widely prescribed traditional Chinese patent medicine, which is clinically applied to treat chronic glomerulonephritis in China and other Asian countries. However, there is still no detailed report existing on its chemical composition at present, which hinders further investigation into its pharmacological activities and mechanism of action. To solve this difficult problem, an ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry method was established to separate and identify the chemical constituents of SYST. A total of 130 compounds were identified or characterized, among which 19 compounds were clearly confirmed by comparing their retention time and mass spectrometry data with those of reference standards. Based on the mass spectrometry data and relevant literature, the remaining compounds were preliminarily characterized. Results revealed that flavonoids, triterpenoid glycosides, organic acids, and alkaloids were the primary chemical components of SYST. The established analytical method has been proven to effectively characterize the chemical constituents of SYST and also provides important reference for clarifying the pharmacodynamic material basis and mechanism of action of SYST.

title: SPEAR: Spatial Epitranscriptomic Analysis by Mass Spectrometry Reveals Localized RNA Modification Remodeling During Glioma Progression
abstract: RNA modifications shape cell identity and disease, yet their spatial organization within tissues has remained largely inaccessible to existing technologies. NGS-based methods can map a limited number of individual modifications with spatial resolution, while liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) provides comprehensive and quantitative coverage of the epitranscriptome from bulk, homogenized tissue. No current approach combines histological resolution, broad modification coverage, quantitative accuracy, and the sensitivity required for microscale clinical specimens. We present SPEAR (SPatial Epitranscriptomic Analysis by mass spectrometRy), a workflow coupling laser microdissection with a redesigned LC-MS/MS pipeline to enable quantitative epitranscriptomic profiling directly from formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue. This combination enables reproducible detection of dozens of RNA modifications from regions as small as 0.1 mm2, establishing a spatial scale previously inaccessible to mass spectrometry-based approaches. Applied to serial mouse brain sections, SPEAR resolved anatomically defined epitranscriptomic signatures across white and gray matter, establishing its spatial resolution and reproducibility in a controlled system. We then applied SPEAR to human diffuse gliomas containing, within individual specimens, both primary low-grade tumor regions and discrete foci undergoing transformation toward higher-grade malignancy. SPEAR resolved this transition directly, revealing a coordinated decrease in multiple methylated RNA modifications specifically within higher-grade regions, a spatially restricted signal that was masked by bulk analysis and reproducibly observed across patients despite underlying genetic heterogeneity. SPEAR establishes spatial epitranscriptomics as a tractable approach for molecular profiling of clinical tissue, providing a platform for biomarker discovery and molecular stratification based on the spatial organization of RNA modifications.

title: Differentiation of tetracycline isomers by cyclodextrin-enhanced ion mobility-mass spectrometry with computational insights
One blotter stamp: Identification of multiple phenethylamine new psychoactive substances and unambiguous differentiation of two isomers
abstract: Abstract In recent years, new psychoactive substances (NPSs) have emerged continuously, often concealed in carriers such as blotter stamps, tobacco, and beverages, posing serious challenges to drug control and forensic identification. In this study, seven phenethylamine substances were detected from a seized blotter stamp using liquid chromatography–high‐resolution mass spectrometry (LC‐HRMS). By comparison with an in‐house mass spectral library, six of them were identified as 25D‐NBOMe, 25E‐NBOH, 25C‐NBOMe, 2C‐E, 25B‐NBOMe, and 25I‐NBOH. The most abundant component exhibited a protonated molecular ion ([M + H] + ) at m/z 330.2068; the relative peak area percentage of this component among the seven identified analytes was approximately 94.6%. Further comparison with the in‐house library indicated that this substance could be either 25G‐NBOMe or 25E‐NBOMe, which were structural isomers of each other. Conventional liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) methods relying primarily on retention time and selected parent/product ion pairs were insufficient to confidently distinguish these two structural isomers, posing a risk of misidentification. Therefore, this study employed HRMS combined with diagnostic fragment ion abundance ratio analysis. It was found that under identical collision energy conditions, the fragment ions at m/z 135.0804 and 193.1223 exhibited markedly stronger responses for 25E‐NBOMe than for 25G‐NBOMe. Based on this, we distinguished the two structural isomers and confirmed that the target substance in the seized blotter stamp was 25E‐NBOMe.

title: Isomer specific spatial distributions revealed by cross-platform ion mobility-mass spectrometry imaging across medicinal plants and fungi
UHPLC-MS/MS method for determination of 1,2-and 1,3-diacylglycerol regioisomers using N,N-dimethylglycine derivatization
Electrochemiluminescence shunt via bi-based co-reaction accelerator for the identification of pentanol isomers
abstract: Pentanol represents an attractive clean-burning biofuel, yet fuel commonly contain multiple structurally similar pentanol isomers that perturb the flash-point and impair combustion performance, necessitating the differentiated identification of pentanol isomers. Herein, we propose an electrochemiluminescence (ECL) shunt strategy that redirects reaction intermediates in a Bi-based bifunctional system, thereby guiding the selective cathodic or anodic ECL emission of luminol for identification of pentanol isomers. In-situ characterization and theoretical calculations reveal that Bi single atoms selectively generate hydroxyl radicals to induce cathodic ECL signal of luminol. In contrast, Bi nanoparticles generate superoxide radicals alongside the electrooxidation of luminol, which triggers an anodic ECL signal. According to the disparate radical-scavenging behaviors of pentanol isomers, a dual-channel ECL sensor array is fabricated. We demonstrate accurate classification of five pentanol isomers by combining principal component analysis clustering with a random-forest supervised-learning model. High-performance biofuels require a well-defined flash point, yet the coexistence of pentanol isomers can introduce ignition-point variations that compromise fuel performance. Here, the authors present an electrochemiluminescence shunt strategy based on a bifunctional catalytic system that exploits the distinct reactive oxygen species scavenging properties of pentanol isomers. The approach generates differential anodic and cathodic luminol signals, enabling their precise discrimination and providing a powerful tool for fuel-quality assessment.

title: Green and fast forensic identification of substituted Cathinones by GC–MS and IR combination
abstract: Synthetic cathinones represent a major group of New Psychoactive Substances (NPS) monitored and seized within the European Union. Acconding to the European Drug Report 2026, substituted methylmethcathinones (MMCs), chloromethcathinones (CMCs), and the emerging bromomethcathinones (BMCs) have become increansingly relevant in European drug seizures. In 2024, MMC, CMC, BMC and N-ethylnorpentedrone (NEP) cathinones together represented more than 80% of the total quantity of NPS reported seized in European Union. While Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) is the gold standard for determining ring substitution, its application is often hindered by the presence of cutting agents in forensic samples, which necessitate laborious purification steps. This study introduces a novel, dual-analytical framework for the fast profiling of 2-MMC, 3-MMC, 4-MMC, 2-CMC, 3-CMC, 4-CMC, 4-BMC and N -ethylpentedrone (NEP) using authentic seized samples provided by the Spanish National Police. We report a high-throughput, eco-friendly GC–MS method using ethanol as a sustainable solvent, achieving baseline resolution of all isomers within a 6-min run time, even in the presence of caffeine as a common adulterant. Furthermore, we describe, for the first time, a systematic FTIR spectroscopic analysis of in-plane C H bending vibrations (1000–950 cm −1 ) as a robust diagnostic tool for discriminating between ortho , meta , and para positional isomers of synthetic cathinones. This integrated approach —combining ‘green’ chromatography for fast screening with definitive FTIR isomeric identification of synthetic cathinones— offers forensic laboratories a reliable, fast and efficient analytical tool to fight the evolving challenges of the illicit drug market.

title: UPLC‐Q‐TOF‐MS/MS Profiling and Synergistic Anti‐HCC Activity of Gallic Acid From Compound Muji Granules Combined With hUC‐MSC‐Exos
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) lacks effective therapies. Compound Muji Granules (MJ), a traditional Chinese medicine, shows potential anti-HCC activity, but its material basis and synergistic mechanism with exosomal delivery remain unclear. Using UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS, 98 compounds were identified in MJ, including 25 blood-absorbed and 23 tissue-distributed components, with gallic acid (GA) as the core active constituent. hUC-MSC-derived exosomes (hUC-MSCs-Exos) were prepared and combined with MJ or GA. In HepG2 cells and rat HCC organoids, exosome-combined treatment significantly reduced IC50, increased apoptosis and necrosis, and inhibited ATP production. Transcriptomic analysis and qPCR revealed regulation of the IL-17/MAPK/p53 axis, with downregulation of MEK1/2, CREB1, and IL17A, and activation of TP53. These findings indicate that MJ exerts anti-HCC efficacy through multi-component synergy, with GA as the main material basis, and hUC-MSCs-Exos enhance these effects by modulating IL-17/MAPK/p53 signaling, inhibiting tumor proliferation and energy metabolism, and promoting apoptosis.

title: Characterization of volatile and non-volatile phenolic compounds in German ciders (type ‘Apfelwein’) by a combined RP-UHPLC-DAD-FLD, HILIC-FLD, and (TIMS)-QTOF-HR-MS/MS approach
abstract: This study screened phenolic compounds in a total of 38 German ciders. An UHPLC-DAD-FLD method was developed to quantify phenolic constituents relevant for ciders, including hydroxycinnamic acids, flavonols, dihydrochalcones, mono- and dimeric flavan-3-ols, and volatile phenols (i.e., vinyl- and ethylphenols), the latter being associated with off-flavors. Additionally, an HILIC-FLD method was employed to analyze tri- and oligomeric proanthocyanidins. Compound assignments were substantiated by (TIMS)-QTOF-HR-MS/MS analyses. Levels of summed quantified phenolic compounds averaged 105.8 ± 54.8 mg/L (28.4–314.3 mg/L), dominated by flavan-3-ols (degree of polymerization, DP 1–7: 54.0 ± 44.1 mg/L; 4.3–213.1 mg/L). Oligomeric procyanidins prevailed, especially those of DP 3 (13.9 ± 10.7 mg/L) and DP 4 (14.9 ± 10.2 mg/L). Hydroxycinnamic acids (23.7 ± 11.1 mg/L; 6.3–45.8 mg/L) and dihydrochalcones (23.1 ± 11.9 mg/L; 0.6–60.4 mg/L) were the next most abundant groups. Vinyl- and ethylphenols were detected at 0.8 ± 0.7 mg/L (0–3.2 mg/L) and 1.9 ± 3.0 mg/L (0–12.3 mg/L), respectively. Higher levels of ethylphenols, 4-vinylcatechol, and caffeic acid were correlated with lower acceptance test rank sums. Overall, the study provides a comprehensive dataset and insight into phenolic compound–sensory relationships in German ciders.

title: Fast LC-MS/MS method to determine seven phytocannabinoids in Cannabis sativa L. inflorescence and medicinal matrices: A new extraction approach using a thymol-based natural deep eutectic solvent
abstract: This work describes the development and validation of an analytical method to determine seven phytocannabinoids in medicinal Cannabis sp. products using LC-MS/MS. The run time was less than 5 min. For the first time, the use of a natural deep eutectic solvent based (NADES) on thymol and butanoic acid as an extraction medium for cannabinoids was evaluated across different matrices (oils, creams, plant extracts, and inflorescences). Analytical performance parameters including linearity, limits of detection (LOD) and quantification (LOQ), precision, matrix effects and accuracy were evaluated according to ICH guidelines. The calibration curves showed coefficients of determination (R 2 ) higher than 0,99. Residual normality was confirmed by the Shapiro–Wilk test and homoscedasticity by the Cochran test. The LOD and LOQ ranged from 10.5 to 94.1 ng mL −1 and from 31.7 to 285.1 ng mL −1 , respectively. Instrumental precision showed a relative standard deviation below 6.1%; intra-assay precision ranged from 0.9% to 6.1%, and inter-assay precision from 3.4% to 9.9%. The results obtained in matrix effect and recovery (accuracy) studies using NADES were compared with those obtained using methanol. For both solvents, most results indicated negligible matrix interference, with superior performance observed for the NADES system. The recovery results were mostly within the limits established by regulatory agencies, with NADES showing the best performance for plant extracts and cream matrices. The developed method proved to be suitable for quality control applications and chemical characterization of several medicinal cannabis-based products, using a universal sample preparation approach.

title: Volatilome Characterization of the Flat White Onion of Fara Filiorum Petri (Allium cepa L.) and Its Differentiation from Other Italian White Onions by HS-SPME-GC-MS
abstract: The Flat White Onion of Fara Filiorum Petri is a traditional Italian landrace that represents the agrobiodiversity and gastronomic heritage of the Abruzzo region. However, its volatile composition has not yet been characterized. In this study, the volatile profile of 31 samples of Flat White Onion of Fara Filiorum Petri and other (53) Italian white onions was investigated by headspace solid-phase microextraction coupled with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-MS). A total of 51 volatile organic compounds (VOCs) were tentatively identified as characteristic of onion aroma. Principal component analysis (PCA) revealed a characteristic volatilomic fingerprint for the Flat White Onion of Fara Filiorum Petri and highlighted a high degree of consistency between the two harvest years, indicating that seasonal variability mainly affected the relative abundance of selected VOCs while preserving the overall volatile profile. Authentication was subsequently investigated using Soft Independent Modeling of Class Analogy (SIMCA). The optimal model correctly recognized 88.9% of Fara samples in the external test set while rejecting all non-Fara onions, achieving 100.0% specificity. These findings demonstrate that HS-SPME-GC-MS combined with chemometric analysis provides an effective approach for the characterization and authentication of the FlatWhite Onion of Fara Filiorum Petri, supporting the conservation of this Italian landrace.

title: B-357 Improving Clinical Utility of Acylcarnitine Profiles: Structural Elucidation of Isomeric and Isobaric Species to Prevent Metabolic Misdiagnosis
abstract: Abstract Background Diagnostic accuracy in mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation disorders (FAODs) depends on the precise identification of acylcarnitine species. Traditional LC-MS/MS approaches often fall short, as nonselective fragmentation fails to resolve isomeric overlaps, leading to potential clinical misinterpretation. By addressing these analytical limitations through refined structural elucidation of the acyl side chain, laboratories can eliminate diagnostic ambiguity and provide the high-specificity results required for effective patient management." Methods Plasma samples of various metabolic conditions were analyzed using reversed-phase chromatography coupled with tandem mass spectrometry to identify the structure. The retention times and mass spectra of compounds were compared to the known profile of analytical standards. Special attention was given to retention time shifts and fragmentation patterns, which were cross-validated with reference standards and/or isotopically labeled compounds to ensure accurate identification. Results We successfully distinguished dicarboxylated acylcarnitines (C7DC–C13DC) from their isobaric hydroxylated counterparts (C12OH–C18OH) by monitoring fragments exclusive to the dicarboxylated side chain. We further resolved the isobaric transitions between hydroxylated species (C14:1-OH to C18:1-OH) and odd-chain species (C15 to C19), a distinction critical for differentiating Long-Chain 3-Hydroxyacyl-CoA Dehydrogenase (LCHAD) deficiency from Very Long-Chain Acyl-CoA Dehydrogenase (VLCAD) deficiency. Notably, we identified both cis and trans isomers for C16:1 and C18:1 in LCHAD patient samples, revealing a novel diagnostic pattern for this condition. Furthermore, our analysis determined that a common C10:2 isomer frequently observed is not the trans-2, cis-4 C10:2 characteristic of 2,4-dienoyl-CoA reductase deficiency (DECRD), but likely a cis,cis-4,7 C10:2 species derived from linolenoylcarnitine (C18:3) oxidation and elevated in Medium-Chain Acyl-CoA Dehydrogenase (MCAD) deficiency. By utilizing authentic standards for retention time matching, we can definitively resolve these isomeric candidates where mass fragments lack distinction, thereby minimizing the risk of clinical misdiagnosis. Conclusion In summary, integrating group-specific fragmentation pathways with stringent retention time matching significantly enhances the specificity of acylcarnitine profiling. By definitively resolving isomeric candidates—such as distinguishing the MCAD-associated C10:2 species from the DECRD-specific marker—these refined strategies minimize the risk of misdiagnosis and facilitate precise phenotypic differentiation. These advancements provide a robust framework for improving the reliability of metabolic screening, enabling more confident clinical management and genetic counseling for affected families.

title: A unified HILIC-FLD-MS workflow for simultaneous peptide and released N-glycan mapping of protein biopharmaceuticals
abstract: Background Quality control of protein biopharmaceuticals has evolved from separate single-attribute assays toward consolidated methods that monitor diverse critical quality attributes in fewer analyses, most often using bottom-up RPLC-MS/MS workflows. Despite its central role in protein characterization, RPLC remains limited in resolving deamidated peptides, retaining hydrophilic species, and separating N-glycoforms, with glycan analysis still often requiring a dedicated HILIC-FLD assay after their release and labeling. Results We introduce a unified HILIC-FLD-MS multi-attribute method that brings peptide mapping and released N-glycan profiling into a single chromatographic run. The method exploits distinct HILIC retention windows of tryptic peptides and RapiFluor-MS-labeled glycans, enabling concurrent monitoring of peptide- and glycan-related quality attributes with minimal interference. In this configuration, HILIC retains the strengths of released glycan analysis, including superior glycan resolution and reliable FLD-based quantification, while broadening peptide mapping beyond the limitations of RPLC. Comparative experiments further revealed fewer temperature-induced in-column peptide artifacts under HILIC conditions and demonstrated that chromatographic separation can induce cleavage of terminal sialic acids, especially in glycopeptides. Significance The proposed method extends HILIC’s role from a dedicated glycan separation mode to an integrated, complementary platform for multi-attribute monitoring in biopharmaceutical quality control. By combining peptide-level information with released glycan quantification, the workflow enables more efficient product evaluation while preserving a reliable readout for glycosylation assessment.

title: LC−MS-Based Chlorine-Signature Query Engine Strategy for Automated Discovery of Phosphate-Containing Metabolites
abstract: Abstract Comprehensive profiling of phosphate-containing compounds (PCCs) in untargeted metabolomics remains challenging due to their high hydrophilicity, poor separation, and low stability, which hampers high-throughput screening from large-scale liquid chromatography−mass spectrometry (LC−MS) datasets. Herein, an LC-MS-based chlorine-tagging strategy integrated with a Chlorine Signature Query Engine (Cl-SQE) was established for the rapid identification of potential PCCs in complex matrices. The novel derivatization reagent, [5-(2-chlorophenyl)isoxazol-3-yl]methyl amine (ClXIMA), can react with phosphate groups on PCCs, such as nucleotides, sugar phosphates, glycerophosphates, and nucleotide sugars under mild conditions, thereby markedly enhancing reversed-phase retention and separation resolution. More importantly, the incorporation of chlorine, identifiable by its characteristic isotopic peak pattern, provides a unique digital signature in the mass spectra. Leveraging these features, Cl-SQE, a data mining program, was developed to systematically and automatically extract candidate PCCs from large-scale datasets. By applying this strategy to liver tissues from a mouse model of cholestasis, 318 potential ClXIMA derivatives were screened out, and 189 metabolites were identified or tentatively assigned. Statistical analysis revealed significant disturbances in nucleotide metabolism, addressing a critical gap in phospho-metabolomic profiling for cholestatic disease and revealing dysregulated nucleotide homeostasis as a potential feature of cholestasis-associated metabolic remodeling. Overall, this platform facilitates the discovery of PCCs in complex matrices and provides new insights into the pathogenesis of cholestasis and other clinical diseases.

title: Comprehensive GC×GC-MS-based Non-Target Screening to Unveil Chemical Profiles of Indoor Dust from Seven European Countries
Comparative characterization of volatile components in commercial Huangjiu with different sweetness classifications using electronic nose, HS-SPME-GC-MS and GC-IMS
abstract: Background Huangjiu has diverse flavor characteristics across four official sweetness classifications, and complementary analytical measurements can provide a more detailed comparison of volatile profiles among commercial products. Methods Commercial Huangjiu samples representing dry, semi-dry, semi-sweet, and sweet types from the same manufacturer were characterized using an electronic nose, HS-SPME-GC-MS, and GC-IMS. Results E-nose responses indicated differences in response patterns among the four commercial products. HS-SPME-GC-MS tentatively identified 56 volatile compounds, while GC-IMS tentatively identified 54 volatile compounds, excluding the internal standard. The two platforms were complementary: GC-MS provided broader compound coverage, while GC-IMS showed enhanced sensitivity toward low-molecular-weight volatile compounds. Comparative analysis revealed differences in volatile composition and identified differential volatile compounds associated with sample separation in the fitted models. Conclusion These findings provide a comparative chemical basis for understanding the quality characteristics of commercial Huangjiu with different sweetness classifications and demonstrate the value of integrating complementary analytical techniques for fermented food characterization and quality evaluation.

title: UPLC-QE-Orbitrap-MS profiling under pathological conditions integrated with symptom-oriented network pharmacology to elucidate the therapeutic basis of Dihuang Yinzi in ischemic stroke
abstract: Objective Dihuang Yinzi (DHYZ) is a classic traditional Chinese medicine formula widely used in the treatment of stroke-related disorders. However, the relationship between its active constituents under pathological conditions and specific symptoms of ischemic stroke (IS) has not been systematically elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the material basis and mechanism of DHYZ by integrating pathological condition-based plasma and brain exposure profiling with symptom-oriented network pharmacology. Methods Ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with Q-Exactive Orbitrap mass spectrometry (UPLC-QE-Orbitrap-MS) was used to identify DHYZ constituents and to profile its absorbed components in both plasma and brain tissue of transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) rats under pathological conditions; symptom-oriented network pharmacology was applied to map brain-penetrating components to stroke-related symptom targets; and molecular docking followed by molecular dynamics simulations was performed to evaluate the binding potential and stability of representative components with core targets. Results A total of 179 compounds were identified in DHYZ. Among them, 64 components were detected in plasma and 28 components in brain tissue of tMCAO rats, with terpenoids (e.g., ursolic acid, catalpol) considered as the main bioactive components. A total of 239 intersection targets, 6 core targets (IL1B, INS, AKT1, IL6, BCL2, TP53), and key pathways (AGE-RAGE, TNF) were screened. Molecular docking suggested that seven representative components (e.g., ursolic acid, catalpol) exhibited favorable binding potential with core targets including IL1B and AKT1 via hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions. Molecular dynamics simulations further supported the stability and activity of the catalpol-target complex. Conclusion This study integrates pathological condition-based plasma and brain exposure profiling with symptom-oriented network pharmacology to investigate the mechanism of DHYZ against ischemic stroke. Among 179 identified constituents, 48 prototypes were detected in plasma and 14 in brain tissue (10 in the infarcted hemisphere). Symptom-target mapping linked IL1B/AKT1/IL6 to motor-speech deficits and INS to amnesia, converging on AGE-RAGE and TNF pathways. This integrated approach-combining pathological-state exposure analysis, symptom-anchored target mapping, and computational validation-provides a more specific mechanistic framework for understanding DHYZ's neuroprotective effects and offers a methodological reference for future TCM formula research from a pathology-anchored, symptom-centered perspective.

title: Simultaneous Detection of Steroid Esters and Multi‐Class Substances in Dried Blood Spots by LC‐HRMS/MS From a Single Spot for Human Doping Control
abstract: The direct detection of intact anabolic steroid esters in blood constitutes unequivocal evidence of exogenous administration and therefore represents a valuable target for anti-doping testing. Dried blood spots (DBSs) offer several practical advantages over conventional blood sampling and may improve the stability of steroid esters during sample transport and storage. Existing analytical methods are primarily dedicated to targeted steroid ester analysis and do not address the simultaneous detection of other prohibited substances within routine anti-doping workflows. The aim of the present study was to develop and validate a comprehensive LC-HRMS/MS method for the simultaneous detection of 15 testosterone, nandrolone, and boldenone esters along with approximately 85 non-threshold substances without minimum reporting level (MRL) in DBS samples, collected using Tasso-M20 devices and cellulose-based DMPK cards. Method validation was performed according to current World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) requirements and included selectivity, reliability, limit of detection, autosampler stability, carryover, and robustness. As proof of concept, testosterone undecanoate was successfully detected in authentic DBS samples following oral administration. The presented method fulfills the current WADA requirements and enables, for the first time, the combined detection of steroid esters and multi-class prohibited substances from a single spot. This approach reduces sample consumption, simplifies laboratory workflows, and represents a practical strategy for routine DBS-based anti-doping testing.

title: Untargeted LC-QToF-MS profiling of the soybean (Glycine max) root-soil continuum reveals spatial compartmentalisation of putative exudate, defence, and iron-acquisition metabolite signatures
abstract: Introduction: .
